Stellen or Stehen? German B1 Position Exercises

Compare placing something upright with its standing position. Practise direct objects, position statements and preposition case cues.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions + writing task

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Try the exercisesWrite your own sentence

Understand the difference

Stellen normally describes putting something into an upright position and takes an object: Ich stelle die Vase auf das Regal. Stehen describes an upright position without a placement object: Die Vase steht auf dem Regal. The preposition also reflects placement versus location in these examples.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not choose only from the English word stand. Ask whether someone places an object or whether the sentence describes where the object is.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Compare the meaning and sentence pattern, rather than choosing by English translation alone.

Worked example 1Ich stelle die Vase auf das Regal.I put the vase on the shelf.
Worked example 2Die Vase steht auf dem Regal.The vase is standing on the shelf.
Worked example 3Sie stellt den Besen hinter die Tür.She puts the broom behind the door.
Worked example 4Der Besen steht hinter der Tür.The broom stands behind the door.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose and conjugate stellen for an act of upright placement or stehen for the resulting position. Try each question before opening the answer. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Bitte ___ die Flasche in den Kühlschrank. (place upright, du)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: stell

The du imperative of stellen is stell; stelle is also possible.

Question 2. Die Flasche ___ schon im Kühlschrank. (position)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: steht

Stehen describes where the bottle is.

Question 3. Wir ___ die Kisten neben das Tor. (place)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: stellen

The subject places the boxes, so use stellen with an object.

Question 4. Neben dem Tor ___ zwei Kisten. (position)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: stehen

The plural subject Kisten takes stehen for its position.

Use it in your own sentence

Describe placing a vase upright and its subsequent position.

Try writing your answer before reading the model below. Other natural answers are possible.

One possible answer

Ich stelle die Vase aufs Fensterbrett. Dort steht sie neben der Lampe.

Check your wording: Stellen takes the placed object; stehen describes its position.

What to practise next

Write a new context for each word. Explain which meaning or object pattern makes your choice natural; some contexts allow both.

Try the gaps again on another day without reading the explanation first. If a choice is still unclear, use the linked grammar foundation before moving to another topic.
